desc:
Amazon FBA inventory and shipment planning keeps your best sellers in stock and your storage costs under control. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your stock, works out what to send and when, prepares shipment plans in Seller Central and sets up restock alerts.

## Why does FBA inventory planning matter?

Fulfilled by Amazon lets you store products in Amazon's warehouses so Amazon can pick, pack and ship orders. It also means your stock levels are tied to your sales. If a best seller runs out, the listing stops selling, and its place in search results can slip while it is unavailable. If you send too much, you pay storage fees and may tie up cash in slow items.

Planning sits between those two problems. It answers how many units to send, which products come first, and when the next shipment must leave your supplier to arrive in time.

## How stock decisions affect sales and cost

Amazon applies restock limits and storage rules that change how much you can send. A shipment that is prepared with the wrong units, missing labels or incorrect prep can be delayed at the warehouse or sent back. Each delay is time the product is not available to buyers.

Aged stock and stranded items add another cost. Stranded stock is inventory in a warehouse with no active listing, so it cannot be sold. Aged stock sits too long and can attract extra fees. Catching both early lets you act with a removal, a listing fix or a price change instead of an unpleasant fee statement.

## What a strong FBA routine includes

- A review of every active SKU, with stock, sales speed and days of cover.
- A flagged list of stranded, aged and slow-moving items.
- Restock quantities worked out from recent sales and supplier lead time.
- Shipment plans with correct units, prep type and labels.
- Restock alerts so you see low stock before it becomes a stockout.
- Fix steps for stranded inventory, listing by listing.
- A stock sheet you can keep updating after we finish.
- A plan for aged stock and storage fees.
- Clear notes on which restock limits apply to your account.

## What we do for you

We start by reading your inventory reports in Seller Central: fulfilled stock, restock suggestions, stranded and aged inventory. Next we compare these with your supplier lead times and cash position so the numbers are practical.

We then build the shipment plans in your account, check units and prep for each product, and tell you what to print and where to attach it. You choose and pay the carrier, and we do not handle your supplier payments. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages grow in the number of SKUs and shipment plans reviewed, and the highest adds a sales-based forecast and a storage fee plan. We do not ship or touch your physical stock.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Keep supplier lead times written down and up to date.
- Restock your fastest sellers before the slow ones.
- Check that every SKU has the right dimensions and weight.
- Fix stranded stock quickly, since it cannot sell.
- Review the inventory dashboard on a regular schedule.

**Avoid:**
- Sending a large shipment of a product that has not proven it sells.
- Letting aged stock sit until fees pile up.
- Skipping prep and label rules because the shipment looks small.
- Ordering from a supplier without allowing for transit time.
- Mixing up SKUs between FBA and your own stock.

## Who this is for

This service suits a seller who keeps running out of a popular product and does not know how much to order. It also suits an owner who just received a storage fee bill and wants to understand it. A seller who splits stock between FBA and self-shipping can use it to get a clear view of both.

## What we need from you

Send your supplier lead times, your target days of cover and a view of your cash for new stock. You invite us as a user in your Seller Central with permission to see inventory and prepare shipments. We never need your password. We do not buy stock, pay suppliers or book carriers for you.
